info.name: TaskFlow API (Milestone 2)
info.description:
Every endpoint of the TaskFlow beta, in demo order, with the expected status and body checks.

Before running: `npm run seed`, then `npm start`. Run the whole collection top to bottom (Run collection). Re-seed before running it again.

exec: // Due dates are relative to today, so the collection works on any day.

item.name: 0. Health and login
item.description: Public routes, then one token per demo user. Run this folder first: every later request uses these tokens.

exec: pm.test("status is ok", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.status).to.eql("ok"); });
pm.test("error message is \"Please log in\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("Please log in"); });
pm.test("error message is \"Wrong email or password\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("Wrong email or password"); });
pm.test("error message is \"Email and password are required\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("Email and password are required"); });

item.name: Body that is not valid JSON

exec: pm.test("error message is \"Request body must be valid JSON\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("Request body must be valid JSON"); });
pm.test("returns a token and never the password hash", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(body.user).to.not.have.property("passwordHash"); });
pm.test("returns a token and never the password hash", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(body.user).to.not.have.property("passwordHash"); });
pm.test("returns a token and never the password hash", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(body.user).to.not.have.property("passwordHash"); });
pm.test("is Karim", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.name).to.eql("Karim"); });

item.name: 1. Projects and members
item.description: Mona creates a project and adds Karim. Hany stays outside it and is used for the 403 checks.

exec: pm.test("has an id and the name", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.id).to.be.a("number"); pm.expect(body.name).to.eql("Postman Demo"); });
pm.test("error message is \"Project name is required\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("Project name is required"); });
pm.test("Karim is a MEMBER", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.name).to.eql("Karim"); pm.expect(body.role).to.eql("MEMBER"); });
pm.test("error message is \"User is already a project member\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("User is already a project member"); });
pm.test("error message is \"Only a project manager can add members\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("Only a project manager can add members"); });
pm.test("error message is \"User not found\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("User not found"); });
pm.test("includes the new project", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.map((p) => p.id)).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("projectId")); });

item.name: Get one project as a member
Get one project as an outsider

exec: pm.test("two members, id/name/role only", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body).to.have.length(2); pm.expect(body[0]).to.have.all.keys("id", "name", "role"); });

item.name: 2. FR1 Create and assign tasks
item.description: US1-1: a manager creates a task and assigns it. Only managers may create; the assignee must be in the project.

exec: pm.test("starts as TO_DO", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.status).to.eql("TO_DO"); });
pm.test("error message is \"Only a project manager can create tasks\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("Only a project manager can create tasks"); });
pm.test("error message is \"Due date is not a real date\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("Due date is not a real date"); });
pm.test("error message is \"Priority must be LOW, MEDIUM or HIGH\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("Priority must be LOW, MEDIUM or HIGH"); });
pm.test("error message is \"The assignee must be a member of the project\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("The assignee must be a member of the project"); });
pm.test("two tasks", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body).to.have.length(2); });

item.name: An outsider cannot read task A
3. FR2 Recurring tasks
item.description: US2-1: a manager makes a task repeat. The next copy is created later, in folder 8.

exec: pm.test("weekly and active", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.frequency).to.eql("WEEKLY"); pm.expect(body.isActive).to.eql(true); });
pm.test("error message is \"Unknown frequency\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("Unknown frequency"); });

item.name: Read the recurrence as a member
4. FR6 Task dependencies
item.description: Task B depends on task A, so B is blocked until A is DONE. Cycles and duplicates are refused.

exec: pm.test("error message is \"Dependency already exists\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("Dependency already exists"); });

item.name: A depends on B would close a cycle

exec: pm.test("error message is \"Circular dependency\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("Circular dependency"); });

item.name: A task cannot depend on itself

exec: pm.test("error message is \"A task cannot depend on itself\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("A task cannot depend on itself"); });
pm.test("isBlocked is true", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.isBlocked).to.eql(true); pm.expect(body.prerequisites).to.have.length(1); });
pm.test("error message is \"Task is blocked\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("Task is blocked"); });

item.name: 5. FR3 Notifications
item.description: Karim was notified when the two tasks were assigned. Only the owner can mark a notification as read.

exec: pm.test("at least the two new assignments", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.count).to.be.at.least(2); });
pm.test("newest is an unread ASSIGNED notification", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body[0].type).to.eql("ASSIGNED"); pm.expect(body[0].isRead).to.eql(false); });

item.name: Another user cannot mark it as read

exec: pm.test("isRead is true", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.isRead).to.eql(true); });

item.name: Unread count went down by one
6. FR5 Filter and sort my tasks
item.description: US5-1 filter, US5-2 sort, US5-3 empty result. A user only ever sees their own tasks.

exec: pm.test("all HIGH, all mine, sorted ascending", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.every((t) => t.priority === "HIGH")).to.eql(true); pm.expect(body.every((t) => t.assigneeId === Number(pm.collectionVariables.get("karimId")))).to.eql(true); const dates = body.map((t) => t.dueDate); pm.expect(dates).to.eql([...dates].sort()); });
pm.test("sorted descending", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); const dates = body.map((t) => t.dueDate); pm.expect(dates).to.eql([...dates].sort().reverse()); });

item.name: No match gives an empty list, not an error

exec: pm.test("empty array", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body).to.eql([]); });
pm.test("error message is \"Sort must be asc or desc\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("Sort must be asc or desc"); });

item.name: 7. FR4 Comments and status workflow
item.description: US1-2: the assignee moves the task. Every change is written to the history. Members comment on the task.

exec: pm.test("error message is \"Task is already IN_PROGRESS\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("Task is already IN_PROGRESS"); });

item.name: An outsider cannot change the status

exec: pm.test("has the author name and a timestamp", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.name).to.eql("Karim"); pm.expect(body.createdAt).to.be.a("string"); });
pm.test("error message is \"Comment cannot be empty\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("Comment cannot be empty"); });
pm.test("one comment", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body).to.have.length(1); pm.expect(body[0].content).to.eql("Started work on this"); });

item.name: 8. Completing a task: the features working together
item.description: One PATCH to DONE triggers three things: the history entry (FR1), the next weekly copy (FR2, through the Observer), and task B becoming unblocked (FR6).

item.name: FR2: next week's copy of task A now exists

exec: pm.test("an open copy of Task A due 7 days later", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); const original = body.find((t) => t.id === Number(pm.collectionVariables.get("taskA"))); const copy = body.find((t) => t.title === "Task A" && t.status === "TO_DO" && t.recurrenceId === original.recurrenceId); pm.expect(copy, "no copy found").to.be.an("object"); const days = (new Date(copy.dueDate) - new Date(original.dueDate)) / 86400000; pm.expect(days).to.eql(7); });

item.name: FR6: task B is no longer blocked

exec: pm.test("isBlocked is false", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.isBlocked).to.eql(false); });

item.name: FR1: history of task A has both moves, with who and when

exec: pm.test("two entries in order", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.map((h) => h.newStatus)).to.eql(["IN_PROGRESS", "DONE"]); pm.expect(body[0].changedByName).to.eql("Karim"); pm.expect(body[0].changedAt).to.be.a("string"); });
pm.test("no longer active", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.isActive).to.eql(false); });
pm.test("error message is \"Please log in\"", () => { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("Please log in"); });
